{"id": "5cca4b17-1246-4e4e-ad08-a09688034131", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Yes, the retention is unbounded, but the cost is negligible at your current volume.**

- **Where logs go:** Bedrock invocation logging writes only to the CloudWatch log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations`. There's no S3 destination, so there's no bucket or lifecycle rule to worry about.
- **Retention:** The log group has no retention policy set, so it uses the default of "never expire". Nothing is ever deleted, and storage grows for as long as logging stays on.
- **Current size:** The group holds about 119 MB. It was created around Oct 16, so it has been running about 5 weeks.
- **Growth rate:** That works out to roughly 3.4 MB/day, or about 100 MB/month. At that rate you'd have about 1.2 GB after a year.
- **Cost:** CloudWatch Standard storage is roughly $0.03 per GB-month, from memory. That puts today's storage at well under a cent per month, and about $0.04/month after a year. I haven't checked current pricing. Ingestion is billed at a higher per-GB rate than storage, but it's a one-time charge as logs arrive, and it's also small at this volume.

**Things to watch:**
- The growth is linear, so a spike in Bedrock traffic would scale it up. Text and video data delivery are both enabled, and prompts and responses are stored in full.
- These logs contain your prompts and completions. An indefinite retention period may matter for data-governance reasons, even though the cost doesn't.

To cap it, set a retention period on the log group, for example 30, 90 or 365 days. Changing retention is a small write operation, and I can run it with your approval. Tell me the number of days you want.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
